title: Let a task name a question id as its blocker, clearing when the question resolves (seq 179d)
description:
opum-doc seq 179, item (d), relayed by opum-agent. Design: opum-doc docs/reference/operator-questions-in-quest-design.md at opum-doc dev (f6390ed8, blob 9f8403c8e836a9af567abec7152123a22abf2240); it is not the main revision.

A task can be blocked by a question: it names the question id, and the block clears when that question resolves rather than needing a second write. Today a task's blocked reason is unrecorded and unverifiable -- QCLI-251 records that the blockers field has no CLI write path at all -- so the first thing this task does is establish what the field ACTUALLY supports, and report that, rather than assuming it can carry a reference.

If the field cannot express a reference as it stands, that is a finding to report to opum-doc, not a design call to make locally.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A task can name a question id as its blocker through the CLI, and the block clears when that question resolves
What the blockers field supports today is MEASURED and reported, including whether it can carry a reference at all, before the shape is built on
A task blocked by an unresolved question is excluded from ready work, and returns when it resolves

implementationNotes: Re-ranked high to medium per the ODOC-480 grooming ruling (opum-ai/opum-doc#1621, 2026-11-04): no 0.16 plan names it. Searched docs/ and .quest/ for a 0.16 plan on 2026-11-04 and found none.

RULING, ODOC-607 (2026-11-18T22:45:04Z): not behind QCLI-447, and needs no write-path decision. A question blocker is derived at read time, so the task reads blocked while the question is open; measure the blockers field before building.

MEASUREMENT FIRST, per the ODOC-607 ruling, taken on dev 53f8d7b2 before any code. (1) SHAPE: blockers is an append-only event array of {kind: opened|cleared, blockId: any non-empty string, actorId, at, reason?, evidence?} (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts:426); blockId is an untyped free string, so it CAN carry a question reference like Q-7, but nothing validates it, tags it as a question, or resolves it. (2) WRITE PATH: there is none - quest manifest advertises no blocker write flag, task edit has no open/clear flag, and the CLI surface (main.ts, command-contract.ts, command-help.ts) has no blocker writer; QCLI-251 was closed as superseded and its final summary says the gap is not fixed. (3) READY: an active uncleared blocker already excludes a task from task list --ready with exclusion reason explicitly_blocked (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts:1315), so the exclusion half of AC3 is true today for any blocker. (4) DATA: 0 records across .quest/tasks/ and .quest/completed/ carry a blocker, and .quest/questions/ does not exist yet, so there are no question records to resolve against. (5) IDS: question ids are Q-<n> validated by ^Q-[1-9][0-9]*$ in src/domain/questions/questions.ts. CONCLUSION: the field can carry the reference, so this is not the report-a-design-gap branch; the work is a write path plus read-time derivation (a block whose blockId names an OPEN question is active and goes inactive when that question resolves or is withdrawn, with no second write), exactly as ruled.

IMPLEMENTED, branch feat/QCLI-448-question-blockers at 5eecc0bb. Surface: quest task block <id> --question Q-N --reason ... and quest task unblock <id> --question Q-N --reason ..., both with --if-revision. blockId is validated against the question grammar rather than accepted as a free string; where the service has a question store, block also requires the question to exist (exit 3 question_not_found) and to be open (exit 6 question_not_open). DERIVATION: a Q-N block is active only while its question is open - answered or withdrawn makes it inactive with the task record byte-identical, so the block clears with no second write (the ruling). A dangling Q-N fails CLOSED; non-question block ids keep their authored open/cleared meaning; an authored cleared event still wins over a still-open question. evaluateReadySet takes the question index as an optional fourth argument so direct TaskService callers and the projection tests are unchanged, and createTaskService injects LocalQuestionRepository so the CLI always supplies it. Manifest gains task.blocked and task.unblocked, with help entries and the overview command list. AC EVIDENCE: AC1 by the new suite tests 1 and 2 (answer and withdraw paths) plus the unblock test; AC2 by this measurement note (committed 23e98c08 before the code); AC3 by the end-to-end ready tests asserting exclusion while open, return on resolution, and unchanged file bytes. VERIFICATION, re-run by the worker on this branch: typecheck green under bun 1.4.4; new suite 7/7; cli-tracker-process 47/47. The implementer also ran integration+domain (220 pass), contract batch (128 pass), lint and layer:check green, and proved test rigor by mutation - replacing the derived predicate with the plain one made exactly the three derivation tests fail while the four write-path tests stayed green. QCLI-411 bun-pin check remains red on local 1.3.14 and green on 1.4.4, unrelated.

DEC-183 ROUND-1 REVISION at 308dbb05, plus the derived-projection follow-up. B1 fixed: docs/specs/quest-cli-dependency-ready-set-and-blocking-design.md is normative and now matches the code - invariant 2 records that readiness reads the question store as well as authored task records; the explicit-blocking model distinguishes an ordinary blocker from a question-named one (open only while the question is open, dangling Q-N fails closed); a Q-N block_id is documented as a reference INTO the question namespace rather than a second one; and same-Q-N reuse on re-block is documented as the deliberate exception to the new-block_id rule. A new Question-named blockers section records the CLI contract and quotes the ruling verbatim. READ SIDE added on the ruling that followed: the raw blockers array is HISTORY, consumers read a derived activeBlockers field once it exists, and the raw array must not be described as the source of blocked - that projection is QCLI-565, filed separately and not stacked on this PR. CITATION CORRECTION: the earlier note on this task attributed the routing to ODOC-607; the text is on ODOC-480, read at opum-doc origin/dev f6390ed883dd551c596a3828a45f08ef37076a2f (2026-11-18T23:54:20Z), and the operator-questions design is cited at opum-doc dev (f6390ed8, blob 9f8403c8e836a9af567abec7152123a22abf2240), not main; the spec carries the same refs. N1: help says --ready OMITS the task rather than naming an exclusion reason no output shows. N2: TaskService.ready() got a test instead of losing its question-store argument, because removing it would let two readiness consumers answer by different rules. N3 and N5: new end-to-end tests for block-unblock-block on one Q-N, block on a WITHDRAWN question, repeat unblock, --if-revision on both commands, and block/unblock reaching COMPLETED and ARCHIVED tasks (both succeed and persist opened/cleared; task view still resolves the retained record). N4, recorded not changed: question blockers are recognised by id grammar alone, so a free-string Q-3 in an existing record would change meaning; exposure is ZERO today because no record carries a blocker and none can be written before this change. N6, recorded not changed: task list --ready now fails on any malformed Q-*.json even when no task names a question, because readiness reads the whole question store; narrowing the read to when a Q-N blocker exists would remove the coupling and is available if wanted. Verification: lore check exit 0 (65 files, 0 errors); typecheck, lint, layer:check, format:check all exit 0; qcli448 suite 13/13 and the affected batch 120/120.

ROUND-2 REVISION, 2026-11-19, and a correction to my own earlier note. F1: the READ SIDE paragraph credited the routing bullet, which says nothing about activeBlockers; it now cites the ODOC-620 extension (a ruling recorded on the ODOC-480 note), drops the word below, and is wrapped in the file style with -- rather than an em dash. F2: the sentence introducing the ruling is scoped - the read-time derivation was ruled by opum-doc, and the write surface (early unblock, Q-N reuse on re-block, fail-closed dangling id, --if-revision) is this repository implementation of it; crediting a local design call to opum-doc misstated design authority. F3: invariant 2 no longer says the question store is read only when a blocker names a question - the code calls questionStatuses() on every evaluation, which my own N6 note said; the sentence now says the store is read on every evaluation, matching src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:1838-1844. N-a: both read-at-the-same-revision sentences now admit the task read and the question read are not one transaction, so a working-tree skew between them is possible. N-b: this record earlier called the ODOC-607 attribution an error; it was not - ODOC-480 records the seq-179 rulings under ODOC-607 and the read side under ODOC-620, so both were right, and the spec now names both. N-c: the description no longer says the design doc is at main; it names opum-doc dev with the blob. N-d: QCLI-565 does not resolve from this branch because #737 landed on dev after the branch was cut - merge order, not a defect; it resolves when the squash lands. The write surface itself is unchanged in this round: no code and no test changed, only the normative spec and this record.
finalSummary: Shipped as opum-ai/quest-cli#736, squash 0f79e063e51187e8e7deaafd173c63853cb02d96, APPROVE from an opus DEC-183 unit after three change rounds. A task can name a question as its blocker through task block/unblock --question, and the block clears by DERIVATION at read time: it is active only while the question is open, so answering or withdrawing clears it with the task record byte-identical. Dangling references fail closed; non-question blockers keep their authored meaning; evaluateReadySet takes the question index as an optional fourth argument. The normative blocking spec was amended in the same PR (invariant 2, the active-blocker model, the block_id namespace, same-Q-N reuse, and a new Question-named blockers section quoting the ruling verbatim from ODOC-480 at opum-doc origin/dev f6390ed8), and it now also points consumers at the derived activeBlockers field that QCLI-565 will add. Review findings N1-N6 were taken or recorded; the round-4 style note R4-1 (two short reflow lines at spec :186 and :247) was accepted as no-change by the reviewer. Verification: typecheck, lint, layer:check, format:check and lore check all exit 0 on the landed head; the new suite is 13/13 and the affected batch 120/120; the derivation is mutation-proven (removing it reds exactly the derivation tests).
